subject: GCP marketplace aggregation change causing split invoice lines — need corrected invoice & payout clarification
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jul 2029 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: GCP marketplace aggregation change causing split invoice lines — need corrected invoice & payout clarification

Hi team,

A seller (Acme Corp) flagged a payout mismatch for July where a single daily usage group was split into two invoice lines with different ledger codes. That split reduced the apparent taxable base and appears to have changed the VAT treatment on our side, which will impact Acme's net payout and Redwood's commission allocations.

I attached a small sample (daily_agg_export_202907.csv) and the seller's invoice (gcp_invoice_202907_acme.pdf). Can you confirm whether there was an aggregation/windowing change on your side between 2029-07-15 and 2029-07-20 that could have caused the split? If so, we need:
- confirmation of root cause and the affected invoice IDs
- a corrected consolidated invoice (or credit note) for Acme and a corresponding accounting adjustment for Redwood
- a target timeline for corrected PDFs (legal requires them for VAT reclaim)

Please loop in the billing team and mark this urgent — Acme has a renewal next week and we need to resolve before payout cutoff.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Finance Ops 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: daily_agg_export_202907.csv (CSV export of daily aggregation sample), gcp_invoice_202907_acme.pdf (seller-facing invoice PDF)

From: GCP Marketplace Billing <gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, jonas@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Jul 2029 12:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: GCP marketplace aggregation change causing split invoice lines — need corrected invoice & payout clarification

Hi Sergio — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments.

We saw an operational change rolled on 2029-07-16 that adjusted the aggregation window for high-frequency meter exports (intended to reduce late-arrival double-counting). That roll changed the grouping key in a small number of sellers which can produce two adjacent lines instead of one in the seller-facing invoice.

Can you confirm the GCP invoice IDs affected (we only have the seller invoice number partial in the PDF)? If you can provide the exact invoice IDs and the affected seller account id, we can:
- produce corrected consolidated invoice PDFs and credit memos
- provide a signed doc describing the cause for your auditor

We will escalate to Billing Engineering once we have the specific invoice IDs. In the meantime we will flag this as Sev 2.

Regards,
Ana Marques
GCP Marketplace Billing Ops

--- Forwarded attachment: daily_agg_export_202907.csv (received) ---

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 08:17:00 +0100
Subject: Re: GCP marketplace aggregation change causing split invoice lines — need corrected invoice & payout clarification

Ana — thanks for the quick note.

Attached is a fuller reconciliation (seller_recon_summary_202907.xlsx) with the three invoices we believe are impacted (ids listed in column A). I pulled the seller account id and the exact invoice IDs from our ledger export.

Quick ask: can Billing Engineering confirm whether the change is an intended aggregation key change (and therefore an accounting-level change we should expect moving forward) or an unintended regression? If it is intended, we need a statement we can share with Acme explaining the permanent change to invoice grouping and the VAT implications. If unintended, we need corrected PDFs and an ETA for credits.

Proposed mutual action plan:
- 48 hrs: confirm the root cause and list of affected invoice IDs
- 72 hrs: issue corrected PDFs/credit memos for affected invoices or confirm that no change is needed
- 5 business days: provide signed root cause statement for legal/audit

Looping in Jonas for technical matching and Marissa for collection impact.

Best,
Sergio

Sergio Alvarez wrote:
> A seller (Acme Corp) flagged a payout mismatch for July...

From: GCP Marketplace Billing <gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Billing Engineering <billing-eng@google.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 15:35:00 +0100
Subject: Re: GCP marketplace aggregation change causing split invoice lines — need corrected invoice & payout clarification

Sergio / Marissa / team —

Billing Engineering investigated and confirmed the 2029-07-16 release included a grouping-key fallback for meters with late-arriving events. That logic was intended, but a subset of metering pipelines failed to normalize timezone offsets for seller accounts with cross-region projects. The result: where we intended to merge adjacent daily lines, we generated two lines (same billing class, different ledger tag).

Impact: ~0.7% of seller invoices in the EU region during the affected window. For Acme (seller id 123456), the invoices you shared (INV-GCP-2029-07-18, INV-GCP-2029-07-19, INV-GCP-2029-07-20) show split lines; the consolidated taxable base should increase by EUR 4,320 on INV-GCP-2029-07-19 which changes VAT by EUR 648 at 15%.

Action we will take:
- Issue credit memos for the affected invoices and reissue corrected seller-facing PDFs (targeted within 4 business days).
- Provide a signed root cause and remediation note for audit.
- Provide a CSV of the corrected ledger lines for Redwood to ingest.

If Redwood needs immediate cashflow remediation (e.g., to avoid a collection hold for Acme), let us know and we can provision a one-time adjustment to seller payout while the paperwork is finalized.

Regards,
Ana Marques
Billing Ops (Marketplace)
GCP Marketplace

Ana — thank you and please pass along to Billing Engineering. This matches our expectation from the ledger. Two quick follow-ups: 

1) We will accept the credit memos and corrected PDFs. Please confirm the exact file naming convention you will use so our ingestion job picks them up without manual intervention (suggested pattern: corrected_INV-{invoiceid}-ACME-202907.pdf).

2) We will need the signed root cause statement (PDF) before our legal team signs any payout remediation acceptance. Please also include the CSV of corrected ledger lines as promised.

Proposed next steps and owners: 
- Billing Ops (Google): produce corrected PDFs, credit memos, and corrected ledger CSV (ETA: 4 business days)
- Redwood (Marissa): update Acme payment schedule and confirm end-to-end payout after credits
- Redwood (Karthik/Jonas): consume corrected CSV and validate ledger mapping; callout any mapping mismatches within 2 business days of receipt

If you can add a short note to the credit memos referencing "aggregation key normalization rollback on 2029-07-16" that will help our VAT team. Once we have the corrected PDFs we will route them to Acme and confirm payout.

Appreciate the quick escalation.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
